To find the physical dimension of luminous efficacy as defined in the problem, we use the provided definition:
Luminous Efficacy = Luminous Intensity / Power.

1.  **Identify the dimensions of the inputs:**
    *   Luminous Intensity ($I$): The problem states its dimension is **Luminosity**.
    *   Power ($P$): Power is defined as energy per unit time. Energy (Work) has the dimension of force multiplied by distance, and force has the dimension of mass multiplied by acceleration.
        $$\text{Force} = \text{Mass} \times \text{Acceleration} = \text{Mass} \times (\text{Length} / \text{Time}^2)$$
        $$\text{Energy} = \text{Force} \times \text{Length} = (\text{Mass} \times \text{Length} / \text{Time}^2) \times \text{Length} = \text{Mass} \times \text{Length}^2 / \text{Time}^2$$
        $$\text{Power} = \text{Energy} / \text{Time} = (\text{Mass} \times \text{Length}^2 / \text{Time}^2) / \text{Time} = \text{Mass} \times \text{Length}^2 / \text{Time}^3$$

2.  **Calculate the dimension of the resulting quantity:**
    $$\text{Luminous Efficacy} = \frac{\text{Dimension of } I}{\text{Dimension of } P}$$
    $$\text{Luminous Efficacy} = \frac{\text{Luminosity}}{\text{Mass} \times \text{Length}^2 / \text{Time}^3}$$

3.  **Simplify the expression:**
    To simplify, we move $\text{Time}^3$ to the numerator:
    $$\text{Luminous Efficacy} = \frac{\text{Luminosity} \times \text{Time}^3}{\text{Mass} \times \text{Length}^2}$$

<ANSWER>Luminosity * Time^
